jurisdictions.name: Central Government
jurisdictions.notes: Central government vertical reservation applies to all central government services, central PSUs, and centrally-aided educational institutions. The 50% ceiling was upheld by the Supreme Court in Indra Sawhney (1992) but EWS was added via 103rd Constitutional Amendment (2019).

sourceLinks.title: Indra Sawhney vs Union of India (1992)

jurisdictions.name: Andhra Pradesh
jurisdictions.notes: Andhra Pradesh has implemented EWS quota. Total reservation exceeds 50% at approximately 60%. State has sub-categorization within OBC groups (BC-A, BC-B, BC-C, BC-D, BC-E).

jurisdictions.name: Arunachal Pradesh
jurisdictions.notes: Arunachal Pradesh has a high ST population. The state provides 80% reservation in state government jobs and educational institutions due to tribal majority population. Most of the population falls under ST category.

jurisdictions.name: Assam
jurisdictions.notes: Assam provides reservations in state government services and educational institutions. EWS reservation has been implemented.

jurisdictions.name: Bihar
jurisdictions.notes: Bihar's current effective reservation is 57% (SC 16%, ST 1%, OBC 30% [EBC 18% + BC 12%], EWS 10%). The baseline reservation (excluding EWS) is 47%, which adheres to the 50% cap. In 2023, the state passed a bill to increase this to 65% (75% with EWS), but the Patna High Court struck it down in June 2024. An appeal is pending before the Supreme Court.
jurisdictions.legalNotes: 65% proposal struck down by Patna HC (June 2024). SC appeal pending. Current status quo (57% Total) remains effective.

jurisdictions.name: Chhattisgarh
jurisdictions.notes: Chhattisgarh provides 58% total reservation in state services. The state has a significant tribal population.

jurisdictions.name: Goa
jurisdictions.notes: Goa has lower OBC reservation compared to other states. EWS quota has been implemented.

jurisdictions.name: Gujarat
jurisdictions.notes: Gujarat provides 49.5% reservation keeping within 50% ceiling. EWS quota has been added over and above the 50% limit as per the Supreme Court ruling.

jurisdictions.name: Haryana
jurisdictions.notes: Haryana provides reservation in state government jobs. The Jat community reservation under OBC has been a subject of legal disputes.

jurisdictions.name: Himachal Pradesh
jurisdictions.notes: Himachal Pradesh provides reservations within the 50% limit. EWS quota has been implemented.

jurisdictions.name: Jharkhand
jurisdictions.notes: Jharkhand has a significant tribal population (26% ST). Current effective reservation is 60%. The state proposed a 77% reservation bill in 2024 but it was returned by the Governor for reconsideration.
jurisdictions.legalNotes: 77% reservation bill returned by Governor (2024). Pending presidential assent.

jurisdictions.name: Karnataka
jurisdictions.notes: Karnataka provides reservation in state services and education. The state has introduced sub-categories within OBC. Total reservation is around 56%.

jurisdictions.name: Kerala
jurisdictions.notes: Kerala provides community-based reservation in state services. Reservation structure differs from other states with SEBC (Socially and Educationally Backward Classes).

jurisdictions.name: Madhya Pradesh
jurisdictions.notes: Madhya Pradesh provides 63% total reservation in state services including EWS. The state has a significant tribal population.

jurisdictions.name: Maharashtra
jurisdictions.notes: Maharashtra provides 52% reservation in education and employment. Maratha reservation has been a significant political issue with multiple legal challenges.

jurisdictions.name: Manipur
jurisdictions.notes: Manipur provides reservation based on its tribal and OBC population composition. The state has unique demographic characteristics.

jurisdictions.name: Meghalaya
jurisdictions.notes: Meghalaya has a tribal majority population (over 86% ST). State provides 80% reservation in government jobs and educational institutions.

jurisdictions.name: Mizoram
jurisdictions.notes: Mizoram has over 94% ST population. The state provides 80% reservation for STs in government jobs.

jurisdictions.name: Nagaland
jurisdictions.notes: Nagaland has a tribal majority (over 86% ST). The state provides 80% reservation for tribal communities in government positions.

jurisdictions.name: Odisha
jurisdictions.notes: Odisha provides reservation in state services and educational institutions. The state has significant SC and ST populations.

jurisdictions.name: Punjab
jurisdictions.notes: Punjab has one of the highest SC populations in India. No ST reservation as there are no scheduled tribes notified in Punjab.

jurisdictions.name: Rajasthan
jurisdictions.notes: Rajasthan provides 50% reservation in state services within the constitutional limit plus EWS. Sub-categorization exists within OBC.

jurisdictions.name: Sikkim
jurisdictions.notes: Sikkim provides reservation based on its unique demographic composition including Bhutia-Lepcha communities.

jurisdictions.name: Tamil Nadu
jurisdictions.notes: Tamil Nadu has 69% reservation (the highest in India) protected under the 9th Schedule of the Constitution. Does not implement EWS reservation for state services.

jurisdictions.name: Telangana
jurisdictions.notes: Telangana inherited Andhra Pradesh's reservation structure and provides around 62% reservation in state services. EWS has been implemented.

jurisdictions.name: Tripura
jurisdictions.notes: Tripura provides reservation based on its tribal population. The state has autonomous district councils for tribal areas.

jurisdictions.name: Uttar Pradesh
jurisdictions.notes: Uttar Pradesh provides 50% reservation plus EWS in state services. The state has a large OBC population.

jurisdictions.name: Uttarakhand
jurisdictions.notes: Uttarakhand provides reservation within 50% limit plus EWS. The state was carved out from Uttar Pradesh in 2000.

jurisdictions.name: West Bengal
jurisdictions.notes: West Bengal provides reservation in state services. OBC reservation includes OBC-A and OBC-B sub-categories.

jurisdictions.name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
jurisdictions.notes: As a Union Territory, follows Central government reservation norms with some local variations for tribal populations.

jurisdictions.name: Chandigarh
jurisdictions.notes: As a Union Territory, follows Central government reservation norms for UT administration posts.

jurisdictions.name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
jurisdictions.notes: Merged UT (2020). Has significant ST population especially in Dadra and Nagar Haveli region.

jurisdictions.name: Delhi
jurisdictions.notes: National Capital Territory with special status. Follows central norms with Delhi-specific OBC lists.

jurisdictions.name: Jammu and Kashmir
jurisdictions.notes: Post abrogation of Article 370 (2019), J&K has its own reservation policy. In 2024, ST reservation was increased from 10% to 20% with the addition of Pahari-speaking people and Paddari tribe. OBC reservation is 8% (different from central norms).

jurisdictions.name: Ladakh
jurisdictions.notes: Ladakh (UT since 2019) has one of the highest reservation policies in India. The 2025 Amendment provides 85% total reservation: 80% ST, 1% SC, 4% for ALC/LoC area residents. Plus 10% EWS = 95% total. Population is predominantly tribal (Ladakhi Buddhists recognized as ST).

jurisdictions.name: Lakshadweep
jurisdictions.notes: Almost 100% ST population. Follows central norms with special provisions for the indigenous population.

jurisdictions.name: Puducherry
jurisdictions.notes: UT with legislature. Has its own reservation structure similar to central norms.
